image_description: A hammerhead shark swimming in an aquarium environment, viewed from a slightly elevated side angle. The shark has a distinctive T-shaped cephalofoil (hammer head) with eyes at the tips. The body is streamlined with visible dorsal and pectoral fins. Several smaller fish are scattered in the background against a dark, rocky backdrop with some green aquatic plants.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic T-shaped hammer head structure characteristic of hammerhead sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark spots corresponding to eyes are visible at the very ends of the horizontal extensions of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The resolution and lighting do not allow for the clear identification of nostrils on the underside or margin of the cephalofoil.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the hammer head appears relatively straight with a slight central curve, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The shark's body tapers smoothly towards the tail and appears thin from the side view, indicating lateral compression.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top of the shark is greyish-white, and the belly area is lighter/white, matching the countershading description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution is insufficient to resolve microscopic skin textures like dermal denticles; the skin appears smooth due to distance/lighting.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A prominent, triangular dorsal fin is visible on the back, positioned roughly in the middle of the body length.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fin on the visible side is broad and triangular, extending outward from the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fin shows the classic shark heterocercal shape with a larger upper lobe compared to the lower lobe.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin texture is unusually smooth and plastic-like, lacking the subtle granularity expected from dermal denticles, though this may be due to image smoothing or water distortion.
Background elements exhibit a painterly, smeared quality typical of AI-generated backgrounds, lacking distinct structural details.

artifact_observations.location: Junction of pectoral fin and body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The connection point of the left pectoral fin to the body is slightly indistinct, blending softly into the torso rather than having a sharp anatomical boundary.
